subject: APAC service evacuation: immediate fallback instructions + validation checklist
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: APAC service evacuation: immediate fallback instructions + validation checklist

Jun —

Quick note from the account team: our telemetry shows a targeted degradation affecting our APAC inference pool (apac-1) that started ~06:40 PDT. Engineering has confirmed the issue is with the cloud provider's regional peering; routing inside APAC remains intermittent. For any latency/errors you’re seeing, the fastest mitigation is to route traffic to a non-APAC region while we maintain the APAC bridge.

Immediate steps (recommended, low-friction):
1) Update your host preference header to prefer us-east-1 or eu-west-1. Set: X-Redwood-Region: us
2) If you pin model versions, switch model endpoint to one of the listed fallbacks (applied at client config): model.redwood.com/v1/serving?region=us-east-1
3) For short-lived sessions, reduce sequence length to <512 tokens to decrease cold-starts during the migration window.

Attached: apac_reroute_quicksteps.pdf (contains curl examples, SDK snippet, and rollback steps).

What I need from you: low-effort validation once you switch (2–5 test calls) and a confirmation in this thread — we’ll track your results and make an ops ticket for any follow-ups. If you want, I can have Rishi jump on a short call to walk through the steps.

Apologies for the interruption — we’re prioritizing your calls.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Jun —

Quick technical follow-up (short list you can paste into CI or runbook):
1) Header-based soft-fail (no DNS change): add header X-Redwood-Region: us (or eu) — this is honored by the gateway layer and will route to the fallback pool within ~500ms. Example curl:

curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: us" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-2028", "input":"Hello"}'

2) KV/prefix cache behavior: switching regions will create a cold KV cache on the new pool. If your workload depends on large context cache hits, consider using the prefetched-rollover approach in section 3 of the attached runbook to warm the cache (we provided a warming script).
3) Guarantees: requests routed to fallback pools will continue to use your account's data isolation. We do not replicate account-level private datasets across regions without a customer opt-in — only non-PII inference metadata is queued for platform observability.

I’ve attached a slightly expanded runbook with the warming script (reroute_playbook_v2.pdf). If you want, I can join the 07:55 call to assist with validation.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Jun —

Thanks for the quick reply. A few operational updates: engineering has opened an escalation with the provider (SUP-4581) and the APAC bridge team is working on a peering anneal. At this stage we expect intermittent recovery signals between 12–18 hours, but we’ll update you as we see steady-state.

We’re not planning any forced rehome of stored customer artifacts; your default account residency remains APAC. Routing to the US/EU fallback only affects the serving plane — no changes to your storage controls.

As a gesture for the impact window, I’ve applied a proactive credit hold for tomorrow’s usage while we stabilize (details to follow from billing). Naomi (CS) will coordinate a 30-min validation session post-cutover to confirm traces and token counts.

If everything’s good on your side after the warm-up tests, we’ll close the ops ticket for your account and follow up with a short post-incident note and the full RCA.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Cache warming reduced cold-starts after ~20 warm-up calls
